comment: BB2001 measurement records (companion to scripts/measure/*.js, mirroring the goldlogs.json pattern). Each record names the src/config.ts constant it informs, so the audit trail runs source -> record -> the constant. Geometry records are in SOURCE pixels (BB2001 renders 640x480). Two independent sources now exist: the public YouTube capture YMmqNpmA60U (measured in-browser with canvas pixel access) and a local ScummVM capture of the Steam re-release (pixel-exact screenshots + a lossless screen recording). Method notes are in docs/research/backyard-2001-video-notes.md; the capture rig is in docs/research/bb2001-capture-setup.md. Every record carries a `status` that scripts/measure/conformance.test.js enforces -- see the statuses block below.

statuses.conformed: BB's value is measured and trusted, and ours is inside the band. The test asserts it stays there.
statuses.known-drift: BB's value is measured and trusted, and ours is OUTSIDE the band. The test asserts the drift is still the recorded SIZE, so it cannot grow or be half-fixed unnoticed. Closing one means editing the record -- a visible, reviewed act.
statuses.awaiting-measurement: BB's value is NOT yet measured (or rests only on a superseded reading). The test asserts our value is unchanged from the recorded snapshot and makes no claim about BB. This is how the pending work stays enumerable instead of becoming folklore.
statuses.note: A recorded finding about the MEASUREMENT rather than about a constant -- a trap, a technique, a dead end. No constant to conform to, but too expensive to rediscover.

schemaNote: Anything carrying a `category` is a record and must carry a `status`. The `sources` block is provenance, not records, and carries neither.

youtube.note: Public gameplay capture, 640x480. Canvas pixel access confirmed untainted, so geometry was measured objectively (dirt/grass boundary scans + RANSAC foul-line fits), not eyeballed. SUPERSEDED FOR PACE: the notes' timestamps no longer map to the stream (an ad or re-upload shifted the timeline), so no play can be relocated by timestamp. The geometry result is unaffected -- it came from a single self-consistent frame.

local.game: Backyard Baseball '01, Steam app 3104970 (2025 re-release ships the original Humongous data untouched), run under ScummVM on macOS

video.gameRectNote: The recording is of a SCREEN, not of the game: the emulator window fills 1920x1440 of the 3024x1964 frame, i.e. 46.55% of the pixels. Located by detectGameRect (bounding box of the largest inter-frame change at a known hard cut) -- NOT by looking for a non-black region, because the surround is desktop wallpaper. Everything measured off this video is read through crop=1920:1440:552:266, which also means nothing outside the emulator window is ever decoded.

screenshots.note: docs/research/bb2001-capture-setup.md predicted ScummVM would write the raw 640x480 framebuffer. It does not -- it writes the scaled window. The conclusion survives anyway: the blit is an exact 3x nearest-neighbour upscale, so decimating the 3x3 blocks recovers the framebuffer bit-for-bit and COLOUR IS EXACT (no YUV round trip, unlike anything read from the video). Measured across all 12: 99.59-99.96% of blocks perfectly uniform, the remainder being ScummVM's OSD toast and the mouse cursor, both drawn at native resolution over the scaled game.

local2.game: Backyard Baseball '01, Steam app 3104970, run under ScummVM on macOS
local2.why: The targeted re-capture prescribed by pace.captureConfounds and step 7 of docs/research/bb2001-capture-setup.md, after session1's natural playthrough failed to isolate any of the three pace shots.
local2.gameRectCheck: blitScore at this rect reads 0.9991-1.0000 across six timestamps spanning the whole file (t=29.5/100/208/300/600), i.e. an exact 3x nearest-neighbour blit throughout -- so `readFrames({crop: gameRect, scale: 3})` recovers native 640x480 game pixels and every coordinate below is in that space.
local2.venue: park (blue plank fence, trees, benches, crowd) -- NOT the backyard-grass venue session1 was played on. That is useful rather than inconvenient: it makes session2 an independent third sample for the geometry records.
local2.continuity: One continuous game segment; no non-game material, so gameSegments was not needed.

physics.note: Peer-reviewed and rulebook sources for the v2 ball. These are PUBLISHED CONSTANTS, not measurements this project made -- which is exactly why they need their own provenance block rather than a `measured` field. Every one was read from the source document, not recalled: `pace.pitchCorridor`'s withdrawn 270ms is what a remembered number costs, and a remembered number with a citation attached is worse, because the citation makes it look checked.

rules.cite: Official Baseball Rules 3.01 (ball: 5 to 5-1/4 oz, circumference 9 to 9-1/4 in). Little League Rulebook 1.09 adopts the same ball.
rules.used: Nominal midpoints 5-1/8 oz and 9-1/8 in, matching the values Nathan normalises on.

atmosphere.caveat: Nathan's 2008 lift paper states 1.23 kg/m^3; his Trajectory Calculator writes '1.225 kg/m^3 (or 0.0767 lb/ft^3)', but 1.225 kg/m^3 is really 0.076482 lb/ft^3. His rounded 0.0767 is what makes his published K come out at 5.509e-3 instead of 5.493e-3. We use 1.225 and record the 0.30% rather than adopting a rounding to make two numbers agree.

aero.cite: Alan M. Nathan, 'Analysis of Baseball Trajectories' (baseball.physics.illinois.edu/TrajectoryAnalysis.pdf), Eqs. 7-11; and 'The effect of spin on the flight of a baseball', Am. J. Phys. 76(2) 119-124 (2008) for the lift experiment and the C_L(S) dependence.
aero.model: C_D = C_D0 + C_D1*(omega/1000rpm); C_L = C_L2*S/(C_L0 + C_L1*S), S = R*omega/v. Fitted by Levenberg-Marquardt to 2015-17 Statcast fly-ball trajectories.
aero.fitScope: Exit velocity >= 90 mph, launch angle 20-35 deg, Tropicana Field (indoor, Nathan estimates rho = 1.194). Velocity-independence of C_D verified only over 60-110 mph.
aero.ignored: Spin decay (Nathan's Trackman-based time constant ~30 s) and spin precession, as Nathan ignores them. A batted ball is airborne under 6 s.

youthExitVelocity.cite: Published youth exit-velocity guidance (multiple coaching/training sources agree): 8-and-under maxima of 45-55 mph off a TEE, with game exit velocity typically 5-10 mph below tee maxima.
youthExitVelocity.confidence: These are coaching benchmarks, not a peer-reviewed dataset. Used to bound the plausible range, not to pin a constant.
youthExitVelocity.note: This is what makes sim.carryVsFence a finding rather than a curiosity: it says a real 4-8-year-old hits 35-50 mph, and the park's shortest fence needs 57.5.

impact.cite: Rod Cross, 'Grip-slip behavior of a bouncing ball', Am. J. Phys. 70(11) 1093-1102 (2002), doi:10.1119/1.1507792.
impact.theFinding: Cross measured the friction force and spin directly and found REAL BALLS DO NOT ROLL WHEN THEY BOUNCE. The contact region deforms and GRIPS when the bottom of the ball momentarily stops; the ball then vibrates horizontally, the friction force REVERSES direction during the bounce, and the resulting spin is LARGER than friction alone would give -- explicable if the normal reaction acts through a point behind the centre.
impact.howWeUseIt: Our grip branch is the idealised rolling-contact limit, so it is a LOWER BOUND on spin reversal against what Cross measured. Recorded as a known simplification rather than left to be rediscovered.
impact.theFormIsDerivable: The 2/7 grip impulse and the v' = (5v - 2wR)/7 result are not taken on trust from anywhere -- they fall out of solving the impulse problem for a sphere (I = 2/5 mR^2, contact one radius below the centre) and were re-derived and numerically verified before use. The MINUS sign is the part that is easy to get wrong from memory.

surfaceRestitution.cite: Brosnan & McNitt (2008a, b) and Brosnan, McNitt & Serensits (2011), Penn State Center for Sports Surface Research, using the 'Pennbounce' apparatus (infrared screens, baseballs propelled at varying angles and velocities).
surfaceRestitution.band: Infield coefficient of restitution 0.4-0.6 -- a ball retains 40-60% of its velocity after the first bounce.
surfaceRestitution.ordering: Skinned (dirt) >= synthetic turf > natural grass. COR is closely related to surface HARDNESS (Clegg hammer Gmax); soil properties affect COR more than cutting height or thatch.
surfaceRestitution.confidence: Read from a secondary summary of the primary papers, not from the papers themselves. Enough to bound our values; not enough to pin one.

frameRate.what: The rate at which the PICTURE actually changes, which is the real precision floor -- not the 60fps the container claims.
frameRate.method: distinctFrameRate over high-motion windows (dupFactor 2.7-3.3, medianRunLength 2-3), corroborated by the inter-frame delta cadence during a live play, which steps in a clean +50ms grid.
frameRate.implication: Every timestamp carries +-50ms of quantisation. A ~3000ms run measurement is +-1.7% (fine); a ~250ms pitch flight is +-20% and needs n>=5 to average down. This is WORSE than the YouTube source's ~33ms, and it is the number summarize({framePeriodMs}) must be fed -- passing the container's 16.67ms would claim 3x the precision that exists.
frameRate.note: Recording at 60fps was deliberate oversampling and it paid for itself here: had the capture been made at the assumed rate, the duplication would have been invisible and every derived constant would have inherited a 3x overstatement of precision.

session2.trap: The session2 working assumption entering this pass was 27-32 distinct fps, i.e. a ~33ms floor. MEASURED, it is 19.5-35 fps with a median near 22 -- a ~45-50ms floor. Feeding summarize({framePeriodMs: 33}) would have claimed ~1.4x the precision that exists, which is the same class of error as the 234px basepath: not a wrong reading, a wrongly-tight ERROR BAR on a right one. 50ms is used for every session2 summarize call.
session2.variability: Unlike session1 (a steady 20fps), session2's rate VARIES 19.5-35 across the file. That variability is itself load-bearing evidence -- see instrument.clockValidity.

clockValidity.what: Does a wall-clock duration read off this capture mean what it says? A 1999 game under emulation could be FRAME-LOCKED -- advancing its logic once per rendered frame -- in which case an emulator rendering below the intended rate stretches every duration and every pace number inherits the stretch.
clockValidity.whyItMattered: session2's home->1B runs read ~4.2s against a superseded ~3.0s prior reading. 3.0/4.2 = 0.71, and session2's distinct rate is ~22fps against a plausible 30fps intended rate: 22/30 = 0.73. The two agree closely enough that 'the emulator is running the game 1.4x slow' was a live and fully sufficient explanation of the entire finding. Shipping the number without testing it would have been the 234px mistake with extra steps.
clockValidity.test: Frame-locking predicts the FRAME COUNT of a run is invariant and its wall-clock varies inversely with the rendered rate. Real-time predicts the opposite. Five tracked home->1B runs spanning 19.9-26.9 distinct fps were measured both ways.
clockValidity.verdict: REAL TIME, not frame-locked. Frame counts spread 45% while wall-clock spreads 30%, so wall-clock is the tighter invariant; and decisively, the HIGHEST-rate run (play-03, 26.94fps) has the LONGEST wall-clock, which frame-locking forbids. The residual spread is per-kid speed rating, which BB2001 genuinely has.
clockValidity.corroboration: An independent check agrees. Re-done frame-by-frame at 33ms on 2026-07-24 (pass 2), superseding the coarser ROI-scan bracket this record first carried: on a 12-tile corridor sheet the ball is still in the pitcher's hand at 53.683, clearly airborne at 53.783, and inside the strike-zone bracket at 53.917 -- a flight of roughly 200-240ms against the ~250ms the YouTube notes measured for a max-arm HEAT. Under a 1.4x stretch the same pitch would have read ~350-420ms, which it plainly does not.
clockValidity.corroborationHistory: The first version of this record read the flight as ~300ms off a three-ROI change scan. The eye read CONFIRMED rather than corrected it -- but only after a background-subtraction track appeared to contradict both (see instrument.background-subtraction, the shadow trap). Recorded because the sequence is the point: two instruments disagreed by 4x and the picture settled it.
clockValidity.nNote: n=5 for the frame-lock test, n=1 for the pitch corroboration. Enough to reject a 1.4x systematic stretch; not enough to certify the clock to a few percent.

backgroundSubtraction.what: The technique added in pass 2 to find the BALL, and the trap it walked into. Companion to pace.tracker-lessons (which covers runners).
backgroundSubtraction.why: Colour-based ball detection is dead in the park venue: a search for small near-white blobs returns 25-30 candidates per frame because the fence, crowd and chalk are all white and all static. The fix is to stop asking what is white and start asking what MOVED.
backgroundSubtraction.primitives: video.js temporalMedian (per-pixel median background) + foregroundBlobs (connected components against it, each reduced to its bounding box's BOTTOM-CENTRE, which is BB's sprite origin). Both are validated against synthetic ground truth in video.test.js on a deliberately hostile clip -- static bright clutter plus two movers of very different sizes -- and the median is what makes it work: a MEAN background smears every transient sprite into a faint ghost that then reads as foreground wherever an actor has ever been.
gotchas: The background window must stay INSIDE ONE VIEW. Sampling across the hard cut to the wide field blends two pictures into the median and the entire frame reads as foreground.

SAME-COLOUR OCCLUSION is silent. Where the ball's colour matches what is behind it, those pixels simply are not detected -- measured on the synthetic clip, a 36px ball is eaten to 24px crossing a 2px white line, which shifts its centroid without ever making it disappear. On real footage that is a ball over the fence, a base, or a white uniform. Pinned by a test.

THE SHADOW TRAP (this is the expensive one). On the plate view the tracker produced a beautiful, clean, monotone descent -- y=134 to y=286 over ~930ms -- and it was NOT the ball. It was a shadow. Taken at face value it would have made the pitch flight ~4x too long and, worse, it would have overturned instrument.clock-validity's corroboration and reopened the emulator-stretch question on false evidence. A frame-by-frame eye read showed the actual ball still in the pitcher's hand at 53.683 and in the zone at 53.917.

In the WIDE view background subtraction alone does NOT isolate the ball: eleven actors are moving, and their extremities throw off small fragments that pass any size filter. Size is not enough there -- see whatRemains.
backgroundSubtraction.whatRemains: Linking blobs frame-to-frame into TRACKS and selecting on motion (fast, smooth, roughly parabolic) rather than on size alone. That is what would make the wide-view ball findable, and it is the specific blocker between here and pace.flyHang.
backgroundSubtraction.lesson: A clean monotone track is evidence that SOMETHING is moving smoothly, and nothing more. It was treated as a validity check in pass 1 (correctly, for runners, because no canned fielder animation produces one) and that reasoning does not transfer to a scene containing shadows. The standing rule -- a tracker brackets and rejects, the picture decides -- is what caught it.

playIndex.what: Where the plays are in the local capture. BB2001 cuts INSTANTLY from the behind-plate view to the wide field view when a ball is put in play, so a scene-cut list is a play index.
playIndex.method: findCuts with crop=gameRect, scale=4, threshold=0.25, run only over the confirmed game segments. Each cut-delimited segment is then labelled plate/wide by median colour in two bottom-of-frame regions (the behind-plate HUD strip paints #004100 there; every wide-field venue paints something else). Calibrated against screenshots 00007/00008 (plate) and 00001/00003/00009 (wide).
playIndex.cutThresholdEvidence: Real cuts score 0.72-0.81 once cropped; ordinary play scores ~0.03. The threshold sits in a wide empty valley rather than being guessed.
playIndex.priorAttempt: An uncropped run at the default 0.3 threshold found 5 cuts in 450 seconds. ffmpeg's scene metric is frame-GLOBAL, so with the game covering 46.55% of the frame every real cut scored ~0.45 -- and only the two strongest cuts in the whole capture cleared 0.3. Cropping first recovered 6.8x more cuts. This is recorded because the failure was silent: a broken index looks exactly like a capture with no plays in it.
playIndex.informs: Nothing in src/ directly. This is the map the pace pass measures against.

session2.method: Same call, unchanged: findCuts with crop=gameRect, scale=4, threshold=0.25 over the whole file. The threshold transferred to a different venue with no retuning, which is a small independent vote for it sitting in a real valley rather than being fitted to session1.

classification.note: From coarse whole-play contact sheets (30 tiles x 200ms per play). The shot list was clearly played -- unlike session1 there are deliberate pop-ups AND left-side balls -- but it also produced five home runs, which are useless for fly hang because the ball never comes down in play.

gameSegments.what: Which parts of the capture contain the emulator, decided WITHOUT inspecting what any frame depicts.
gameSegments.method: ScummVM blits 640x480 at an integer factor, so inside its window every group of 3 consecutive rows is pixel-identical; native desktop content is not. blitScore samples row-triples (rows, not columns -- yuv422p subsamples chroma horizontally, so column triples break at block boundaries while row triples survive exactly) and scores ONLY samples where the image varies vertically, since a flat region passes the triple test trivially and would let a blank window impersonate the game.
gameSegments.note: 463 samples at 2s spacing, no ambiguous ones and no overlap between the classes. 737s of game material -- 2.3x what an earlier hand-built index had assumed was in scope. Measurement is confined to the two game runs.

landingDisc.what: How to time a BB2001 fly ball, after tracking the ball itself failed twice.
landingDisc.finding: BB draws a big saturated-green ellipse on the grass at the predicted landing spot for exactly as long as the ball is in the air. Measured: disc RGB (44-58, 207-223, 26-40) against grass that tops out around g=165, so `g>=190 && r<=90 && b<=70` separates them with no overlap at all. It appears on the frame of contact and vanishes on the frame the ball reaches a glove or the ground.
landingDisc.whyNotTheBall: The ball is ~5px, and in the wide view BB frequently draws it into a picture-in-picture inset at the top of the frame instead of onto the field, so for much of a high fly there is no ball on the field to track. The disc is ~96x40px, always on the field, and uniquely coloured. It is the better instrument by every measure.
gotchas: There are TWO green things. The landing disc is large and belongs to the ball; the active fielder's glow is smaller and moves with him. Taking all green pixels together blends them and the lifetime runs past the catch (play-19 read 3.02s that way against an eye-verified 2.85s).

The disc MOVES. It tracks the updating landing prediction, so pinning it to its first bounding box truncates the measurement -- play-06 read 2334ms that way when the disc was plainly still on screen at 2680ms, and the true value is 3100ms.
The disc is OCCLUDED. A fielder standing on it can hide most of it for several frames, which breaks a naive continuous-run detector -- play-11 read 3084ms that way against an eye-verified 5075ms.
All three of those produced clean, plausible, wrong numbers. Every sample in pace.flyHang was therefore read by eye off a zoomed sheet; the detector's role was to say where to look.

pipPitchIndex.what: How to find every pitch in a plate stretch, after three other discriminators failed.
pipPitchIndex.finding: The HUD's BALLS/STRIKES pips are the only unambiguous pitch marker. A resolved pitch lights one and nothing else does. Mound motion does NOT work: the pitcher tosses the ball to himself on a loop while the human deliberates, producing identical bursts. Zone colour does not work: the strike-zone fill is dirt-brown and a white-blob search returns only crop-boundary artifacts.
gotchas: THE ODD-WIDTH TRAP, and it cost the most. The capture is yuv422p, which subsamples chroma HORIZONTALLY, and ffmpeg emits ZERO frames for an odd-width crop -- no error, no warning, an empty buffer. A 435px-wide pip crop silently returned nothing, which read exactly like 'this capture has no taken pitches' and briefly became a recorded conclusion. Widening it to 436 showed 17 of 20 plate stretches contain count changes. ALWAYS use even crop width and height on this source.

Do not run the scene metric over the pip strip across the WHOLE file: during live plays BB collapses the HUD to a mini scoreboard with no count at all, so every view cut registers as a pip change. Restrict to plate stretches.

Pitch-to-pitch cadence is NOT the between-pitch constant. Measured gaps are 10.7-11.6s, because the human deliberates over the SWING cards while batting exactly as they do over the pitch cards while pitching. session1's confound was assumed not to apply to a human-batting capture; it does.

captureFidelity.what: Why session2 cannot set pitch timing, and what a usable capture must carry.
captureFidelity.theGap: session2's real-time fidelity was ASSUMED, never measured. Nothing in the file distinguishes 'the game did X in 250ms' from 'the recording compressed 2s into 250ms' from 'the emulator ran the animation faster than the game intends'. The capture guide's ffv1/60fps rules protect image quality; none of them bound the clock.

whatIsAndIsNotEstablished.established.renderRate: The game draws a steady ~22fps throughout: wide play 22.18, plate idle 22.69 (distinctFrameRate, scale 4, n=120 each). The pitch corridor is not an exception, so there is NO frame-dropping during the pitch.
whatIsAndIsNotEstablished.established.ballIsBarelyDrawn: CORRECTED 2026-07-26. This previously read 'the ball SPRITE appears in only ~5 frames of a pitch'. It does not. The ball is drawn from release; it is ~5px and is simply LOST IN THE GRASS at low magnification. Read at >=2x it is visible leaving the pitcher's hand. The error mattered: it made a ~1230ms flight look like ~200ms, and it is the single mistake behind every pitch-timing number this project has produced.
whatIsAndIsNotEstablished.notEstablished.rushHypothesis: An earlier draft of this record claimed ~5 rendered positions PROVED a rushed capture. It does not. Running pitchFidelity over the corridor returns maxSteps 9-13 across a 300ms window -- fully consistent with 22fps and NOT a rejection. The claim was withdrawn before it could become the next unchecked number.
whatIsAndIsNotEstablished.notEstablished.uniformity: Whatever affects the pitch does not obviously affect everything: runner legs in the same capture measure plausibly (~4.2s home->1B). A non-uniform artifact is exactly what would hide from a whole-capture sanity check, which is why per-quantity fidelity gates exist now.

requiredOfTheNextCapture: A millisecond stopwatch IN FRAME beside the game window. Elapsed time then comes off pixels, not container metadata. Use a NATIVE stopwatch: a browser tab can be throttled, which would defeat the purpose.
Gate with video.js clockFidelity before reading any timestamp. timeScale must be ~1.0.
Gate with video.js pitchFidelity. It REJECTS, it does not certify -- the bound is loose because the pitcher's arm and the target shadow animate in the same corridor.
HEAT and SLOWBALL thrown FROM THE MOUND so the pitch card is on screen (classificationGroundTruth).
captureFidelity.scopeOfTheStopwatch: It proves the RECORDING is real-time. It does NOT prove the emulator runs the game at authentic speed -- a faithful recording of a too-fast emulator passes. What it does settle is sharper and sufficient: whether the pitch ON SCREEN, in the session where it is perceived as ~2s, actually took ~2s.
captureFidelity.supersededHypothesis: DEAD: 'session2 is rushed ~7x'. Re-read at magnification, session2's flight (>=750ms) agrees in order with the stopwatch-gated capture (1230ms). The apparent 7x was the low-magnification reading error on both sides of the comparison, not an emulator artifact. Never shipped -- withdrawn before commit -- and it should not resurface.

projectionType.what: Is BB2001's field an affine squash of the diamond (like ours) or true perspective? A diamond is a SQUARE, so its 4 bases are a square's corners; affine maps preserve diagonal bisection, perspective maps do not.

measurements.method: RANSAC fit of the white chalk foul lines (occlusion-robust), bases from dirt/grass boundary scans so standing fielders read through.

measurements.venue: backyard-grass (pool, shed, red roof) -- the venue every play in the local video is on
measurements.method: Compact white-blob detection at NATIVE resolution (pixel-exact, no scaling), cross-validated across three frames of the same venue: a base cannot move between frames, a fielder can. Two symmetric candidates at y~283 appeared in only one frame and were correctly rejected as fielders; the four that persisted are the bases. Confirmed visually by overlay.
measurements.internalChecks: 1B and 3B land on the SAME y (310.9) without being constrained to; home x 320.3, 2B x 318.0 and the 1B/3B midpoint x 320.45 all agree within 2.5px. Under an affine map opposite legs would be equal -- home-1B is 198.58 and 2B-3B is 176.43, an 11.75% spread, which is an independent perspective signature that does not use the diagonal test at all.

measurements.venue: park (blue plank fence, trees, benches) -- a THIRD venue, distinct from both prior sources
measurements.frame: 26 wide frames spread across the whole capture, native 640x480
measurements.method: White-blob detection clustered ACROSS frames, keeping only blobs that persist at the same centroid: a base cannot move, a fielder can. Two naive variants were tried and rejected first -- 'biggest blob' locks onto base+white-sock merges (n=216px vs home plate's 87px), and 'modal centroid' locks onto chalk-line fragments (a 2x16px sliver at (330.8,439.5)). Both were caught by the internal symmetry checks below failing, then confirmed by rendering the candidates as boxes over a real frame and looking.
measurements.internalChecks: 1B and 3B land on the SAME y (311.2) unconstrained; home x 318.2, 2B x 317.4 and the 1B/3B midpoint x 318.75 agree within 1.4px; foul-line slope asymmetry is 0.71%. Opposite legs are 202.3 vs 178.5 (12.46% spread) -- the same independent perspective signature, on a third venue.
measurements.visualConfirmation: All four derived positions rendered as boxes over the t=208 frame land on the pillows, including the two that were partly behind fielders.

projectionType.nNote: Three INDEPENDENT sources, three different venues, three different measurement techniques, all far past the threshold (11.6x, 5.9x and 6.4x). Perspective STRENGTH differs by venue (0.141 vs 0.082), so it is a per-venue camera property, not one global constant -- worth knowing before anyone tries to model it with a single number.
projectionType.driftNote: Our projection maps y 1:1 -- a pure horizontal pinch with NO vertical foreshortening, so its diagonal-midpoint gap is exactly 0 and it is affine by construction. Matching BB would mean a render-only y'=f(y) plus a matching inverse in unproject, keeping the sim flat so geometry.ts, clampToField's convexity argument and the goldlog stay untouched.
projectionType.v2: CLOSED in v2 by the renderer change: a three.js PerspectiveCamera IS true perspective, so the diagonal-midpoint gap is nonzero by construction (21.7px on RIGS.FIELD against this record's 3px affine threshold). Asserted renderer-free in src/v2/render/cameraCues.test.ts by projecting the four bases through the preset's matrix -- no pixels, no screenshot diff. The v1 constant and this drift remain live and asserted for as long as v1 ships.
projectionType.deliberate: This drift is a KNOWN PRODUCT DECISION, not an oversight. Our flatter view is a style choice; adding perspective is a large visual change gated behind the graphics phase and does not affect pace.

foulSlope.what: Near-field lateral foreshortening: horizontal run per unit of depth along the foul lines from home.

measurements.method: RANSAC fit of white chalk foul-line pixels, refit on inliers.
Derived from the four cross-validated base positions via lib.js affinity().
Same as session1: lib.js affinity() over four persistence-clustered, visually confirmed base positions.

supersedes.why: The old record read a 0.24% agreement between two sources as 'BB's foul slope is 1.24, full stop', and concluded our 1.2 was a real 3.2% drift because the gap was 14x that spread. The third venue breaks that reading: the park field measures 1.1974, so the 0.24% agreement was two venues that happened to be similar, not a global constant. BB's foul slope is a PER-VENUE camera property spanning at least 1.197-1.241 -- exactly the conclusion geometry.projection-type had already reached independently about perspective STRENGTH.
supersedes.lesson: n=2 agreeing tightly is not the same evidence as n=2 sampling the space. Both prior sources were fenced-stadium-ish fields; neither tested the variation the third one found. The tight spread was real and the inference from it was wrong.

foulSlope.nNote: Three sources, three venues, three techniques. The 3.7% spread BETWEEN venues is 5x the worst within-venue left/right asymmetry (0.71%), so the variation is a property of BB's per-venue cameras and not measurement noise.
foulSlope.conformNote: Our 1.2 sits INSIDE the measured band [1.1974, 1.2414], 0.2% off the park venue and 3.2% off the two stadium-ish ones. Since we render one slope for all three of our venues, sitting near the shallow end of BB's range is a defensible single choice and there is nothing to fix. What we still lack is the DEPTH compression, which is a separate record (geometry.projection-type) and unaffected by this.

fieldScale.what: How BIG the diamond is drawn, as a fraction of the frame. Normalised by frame HEIGHT: that is the dimension the field is squeezed in, and it is the one comparable across BB's 4:3 and our 3:2.
fieldScale.why: Reported as 'why is the field smaller in our game vs in BB from the fielding and running view'. The complaint is real and the cause is not what it looks like -- our KIDS are correctly sized against the frame (an outfielder is ~9% of frame height, BB's ~8-9%). The diamond around them was too small, so the players dwarfed the field.
fieldScale.method: No new capture needed. geometry.projectionType already carries pixel-exact base positions for three BB venues, measured by persistence-clustered white-blob detection at native 640x480 and visually confirmed. basepath = |home - first| from those. Ours is DERIVED from geometry.ts through art/projection.ts, so it measures what is actually drawn rather than what a constant says.
fieldScale.nNote: The same three venues geometry.projectionType and geometry.foulSlope rest on. The stadium venue is a clear outlier at 52.3% -- BB's camera distance is per-venue, exactly like its perspective strength and foul slope -- so the two LOCAL venues (41.4, 42.1) are the honest target and the band's top is not something to chase.
fieldScale.driftNote: Ours is 34.0% against BB's 41.4% -- still 19% short, and the shortfall is STRUCTURAL rather than a tuning choice. Four constraints pin ZOOM at 1.28: FIELD_BOTTOM_Y (sim y 600) must land at or above the canvas bottom (639.8), the catcher's spot (540) must stay above HUD.STRIP.TOP (563 < 568), the fence needs headroom for its own structure plus the skyline band (mid-arc lands at 110), and the basepath is maximised subject to those. Raising the zoom past that puts the catcher behind the scoreboard or the foul ground off the canvas.
fieldScale.whatWouldClose: Reclaiming vertical space rather than zooming further. Our full-width HUD strip eats 11% of frame height where BB's wide-view HUD is a small corner box; that alone is most of the remaining gap. Shrinking FIELD_BOTTOM_Y would also buy room, but it is a SIM constant (clampToField) and would move the goldlog.
fieldScale.whyNotWider: A non-uniform zoom -- x scaled more than y -- would buy the width our 3:2 canvas is short of against BB's 4:3, and the width gap is the bigger one (33.3% of frame width against BB's ~48%). It is rejected on purpose: it would change the DRAWN foul slope from 1.2 to ~1.35, outside the [1.1974, 1.2414] band geometry.foulSlope is conformed to. That record was measured off BB's screen pixels, so breaking it on screen breaks it for real.
fieldScale.renderOnly: This is a camera change and NOTHING else. The sim stays in flat 960x640 space, so LIVE.RUNNER_SPEED, the conformed home->1B time, clampToField's convexity argument, every systems/ test and both goldlog fingerprints are untouched -- verified byte-identical after the change. It is also still AFFINE (a uniform scale composed with the existing pinch), so geometry.projectionType's drift is unchanged and its conformance assertion still passes.
fieldScale.sideEffect: Fielder height went from 33% of a basepath to 26% (BB: ~20%). depthScale is deliberately NOT multiplied by ZOOM -- the field grows and the kids do not, which is the half of the complaint that was about proportion rather than size.
fieldScale.v2: CLOSED in v2 by the renderer change. A real PerspectiveCamera has independent elevation, distance and FOV where the affine projection had a single ZOOM scalar pinned by four simultaneous layout constraints -- so the drift here was structural, not a tuning choice. src/v2/render/cameraCues.ts RIGS.FIELD is SOLVED to 41.4% (elevation 40deg, distance 155ft, fov 46) and src/v2/render/cameraCues.test.ts asserts it by projecting the four bases through the preset's matrix. The v1 constant and this drift remain live and asserted for as long as v1 ships.

render.note: v2-only records: findings about the three.js renderer that have no v1 equivalent because v1 had no camera, no lights and no depth.

characterPresence.what: BB2001's field framing and BB2001's character size are JOINTLY UNSATISFIABLE once the field is modelled at real scale. Recorded so the contradiction is not rediscovered as a bug.
characterPresence.why: v2 moves the field to real units (60ft basepaths, 3.6-4.4ft kids) because v1's compressed outfield was the root cause of the balance failure -- see the v2 block on geometry.fieldScale and src/v2/sim/field.ts. Real units then make the two existing records arithmetically incompatible.

derivation.fieldScale: geometry.fieldScale: BB's basepath spans 41.4% of frame height (local venues, n=2).
derivation.characterSize: A BB fielder stands ~8-9% of frame height (recorded in geometry.fieldScale's `why`).
derivation.note: 0.085 * 480 / 198.6 = 0.205 basepaths. A real 4ft kid on a real 60ft basepath is 4/60 with foreshortening, measured at 0.045-0.059 across depths. Matching BB would need a FOURTEEN FOOT child -- taller than the 8ft outfield wall they are meant to rob home runs at.

characterPresence.whyBBCouldDoIt: BB2001's field was a painted backdrop with no physics behind it, so its proportions cost nothing. v2's ball obeys real gravity over real distances, and that is precisely the balance fix -- so the field cannot be shrunk back to make the kids look big.

resolution.cameraSplit: src/v2/render/cameraCues.ts ships TWO wide rigs. FIELD conforms to geometry.fieldScale and is the establishing shot (half-inning starts, wide resets, replays). PLAY is where the game actually lives: same 40deg elevation so a cut never shifts the foul slope, at 115ft instead of 155ft. PLAY deliberately does NOT conform, and that is recorded here rather than left as an unexplained inconsistency.
resolution.characterScale: src/v2/render/ProxyCharacter.ts CHARACTER_SCALE = 1.6 -- a RENDER-ONLY exaggeration drawing a 4ft kid as 6.4ft. Chunky-cartoon, still clear of the 8ft fence, the backstop and the foul poles. It must never leak into src/v2/sim/**: catch radii, reach, stride and collision stay real feet, and scripts/v2/purity.lint.test.js keeps the sim from importing render/.
resolution.residual: Even at 1.6x on the PLAY rig a kid reads ~5% of frame height against BB's 8-9%. The remaining presence has to come from character DESIGN -- saturated colour, heavy contour, readable silhouette -- not from more size. That is a brief for the commissioned models, and it is why the Look Spike exists. CORRECTED 2026-07-30: this 5% was aspirational when written. The rig was 3.400ft against a claimed 4.0 and the proxy drew 3.105ft, so the real figure was 3.90%. It is 5.02% now that both are fixed -- see render.rigHeight.

rigHeight.what: The canonical rig claimed 4.0ft and was 3.400ft. Recorded because the error class -- a constant asserting a number that nothing computes -- is the one this whole instrument exists to catch, and because it was about to be printed at the top of a commission brief.
rigHeight.found: src/v2/render/skeleton.ts set REFERENCE_HEIGHT_FT = 4.0 while the SKELETON table's parent-relative offsets summed to a HeadTop_End of 3.400ft -- 15% short, and BELOW the 3.6ft floor of the height band the same file defines for every character. Nothing summed the table, so every consumer read the constant and trusted it.
rigHeight.whyItMattered: docs/v2/animation-brief.md opens with '1 unit = 1 foot, the reference kid is 4.0 ft tall' and ships skeleton_recess_v1.glb alongside it. Stride length, foot plants and dive travel are authored in absolute feet against the rig the animator is handed, so a 3.4ft rig buys 35 clips whose every distance is 17% wrong -- against a sim that works in real feet -- and the error surfaces after the invoice.
rigHeight.secondError: The PROXY was shorter again: ProxyCharacter's head sphere used a hardcoded radius of 0.46 with no relation to the crown bone, topping out at 3.105ft. So a kid declared 4.0ft drew 4.97ft on screen at CHARACTER_SCALE 1.6 rather than 6.40ft.

consequence.claimed: ~5% of frame height on the PLAY rig
consequence.nowTrue: 5.02%. PLAY sits 115.0ft out at 46deg vertical FOV, so the frame is 97.63ft tall at the focus; a 4.0ft kid drawn at 1.6x is 6.40ft, foreshortened by cos(40deg) to 4.90ft = 5.02% of frame, i.e. 40.2px on an 800px viewport. The brief's 'about 5% of screen height' and 'readable at 40px tall' are only simultaneously true after the fix.

rigHeight.fix: The whole bone table was rescaled by 4.0/3.4 and re-rounded so the chain sums to exactly 4.000 (1.671 + 0.212 + 0.235 + 0.235 + 0.188 + 0.165 + 1.294). Proportions of the BONE CHAIN are unchanged -- the Head joint still sits at 32.35% of the crown, against the contract's '~30%'. ProxyCharacter now DERIVES its head radius from the crown, so the drawn silhouette lands on HeadTop_End by construction, and its other primitive dimensions were scaled by the same factor.
rigHeight.correctedClaim: That 'proportions are unchanged' sentence was true of the BONE CHAIN and was read as a statement about the DRAWING, which it was not: the drawn head sphere was 36.97% of body height, not 32.35%, because HEAD_RISE 0.75 reached the crown by hanging the sphere below the Head joint. Corrected 2026-07-30 -- see render.proxySilhouette. The class of error is this record's own: a number nothing computed, believed because a nearby number was checked.
rigHeight.pinnedBy: src/v2/render/skeleton.test.ts asserts crownHeightFt(SKELETON) === REFERENCE_HEIGHT_FT exactly, that the reference sits inside [HEIGHT_MIN_FT, HEIGHT_MAX_FT], and -- the one that actually failed -- that a built ProxyCharacter's world bounding box tops out at heightFt * CHARACTER_SCALE within 2%. scripts/v2/validate-models.mjs applies the same height rule to every delivered model.
rigHeight.alsoFixed: ProxyCharacter defaulted body.height to 1.0, the TOP of v1's authored 0.82-1.0 band, so the six kids in characters.ts with no authored height were each the tallest child in the game at 4.4ft. The default is now the band centre, which maps to exactly 4.000ft.
rigHeight.informs: src/v2/render/skeleton.ts REFERENCE_HEIGHT_FT and SKELETON, src/v2/render/ProxyCharacter.ts CHARACTER_SCALE

proxySilhouette.what: The rig summed to the height it claimed and the proxy STILL drew a bobblehead. Four drawn-silhouette errors that the bounding-box test could not see, because it measures a single point (the topmost vertex) of a single fixture (bald, no accessory).

found.head: The head sphere drew 1.479ft -- 36.97% of body height -- against a bone chain that puts the head at 32.35% and a commission brief that tells the animator '~30%'. HEAD_RISE 0.75 put the sphere's centre only 0.75 radii above the Head joint, so it reached the crown by hanging below the joint. The height test passed the whole time: the sphere's TOP was always right.
found.torso: ball(at, r, scale)'s third argument is a dimensionless SCALE, and the torso handed one axis a LENGTH: x and z divided the desired half-extent by the 0.424 sphere radius, y did not. The trunk drew 0.49ft tall against 1.18ft wide.
found.neck: Nothing was bound to the Neck or Spine2 bones at all, leaving 0.228ft of open air between a torso ending at 2.293 and a head starting at 2.521 -- invisible only because the head was big enough to cover it. It also meant every head-turn key in the clip library drove nothing visible.
found.hair: No hair style and no accessory was measured by any test, because the fixture is hair:'bald', accessory:'none' -- 44 of 44 combinations unmeasured. That hid an afro standing 14.2% of body height above HeadTop_End, and a `spiky` whose absolute-sized cones sat INSIDE the skull, collapsing one of eleven silhouettes onto another.

proxySilhouette.whyItMattered: The proxy is not a placeholder that goes away. It is the acceptance test for the skeleton spec, the permanent LOD3, the fallback when a model fails to load, and -- until the commissioned models land -- the ONLY character anyone sees. render.characterPresence's residual argues the missing presence must come from character DESIGN: 'saturated colour, heavy contour, readable silhouette'. Silhouette was the one of the three that was measurably wrong, on the surface where the animation brief's acceptance criteria are judged.
proxySilhouette.fix: HEAD_RISE = 1.0, which needs no justification beyond its arithmetic: the centre sits exactly one radius above the Head joint, so the sphere spans Head -> HeadTop_End, the segment the bone table already calls the head. The radius is derived against headH as well, so a headH 1.08 kid no longer draws its crown 1.5% above the bone that defines its height. A blob() helper states ellipsoids in half-extents so no axis can be handed the wrong kind of number, and the torso is bounded by bind-pose landmarks (shoulder joint, pelvis) instead of magic numbers. A neck capsule bridges Spine2 -> Head on the Neck bone. Hair and accessories were re-anchored to the head SPHERE rather than the Head BONE first -- provably a no-op at the old HEAD_RISE, and mandatory, since anchoring off the bone meant changing HEAD_RISE would have slid every cap a quarter-radius down the skull and put a bald patch on eleven hair styles. Hair keeps a headroom budget (HAIR_HEADROOM_FRAC) instead of a hard cap, because height is defined on the BONE and an afro that stops at the skull is not an afro.
proxySilhouette.alsoFixed: The proxy had nothing at all on the front of its head, so at the animation review page's own criterion 4 ('readable at 40px tall') a kid was rotationally ambiguous and a clip authored 180 degrees backwards would have looked fine. Two eyes, two brows and a nose, on the Head bone at 8x6 segments: a FACING CUE, not a face. Expression stays where the contract puts it -- the face_atlas texture on the delivered models -- and there is deliberately no mouth. The brows were removed once and restored -- see render.proxyFace, which is where the face's own errors are recorded.
proxySilhouette.pinnedBy: src/v2/render/skeleton.test.ts 'the proxy draws a kid, not a bobblehead': the silhouette budget across all 11 hair styles x 4 accessories (both a ceiling and, for the styles made of height, a FLOOR -- a ceiling alone cannot see a spike buried in the skull); solid-span ray casts through the merged buffer for body continuity, accumulated by winding depth because the parts deliberately interpenetrate; the drawn head span asserted against the BONE span so the drawing and the brief cannot diverge again; and the crown checked on all 30 kids, not the average one. Every one of those was verified to FAIL against the code it replaced.
proxySilhouette.informs: src/v2/render/ProxyCharacter.ts HEAD_RISE, and HAIR_HEADROOM_FRAC (which now lives in src/v2/render/skeleton.ts, re-exported from ProxyCharacter, so scripts/v2/validate-models.mjs can enforce the same headroom on a DELIVERED model -- enforcing it only on our own stand-ins was checking the one character nobody is paid to make)

proxyFace.what: The facing cue added by render.proxySilhouette was itself half invisible. Recorded separately because the errors are a different class: not 'the number nothing computes' but 'the feature nobody looks at', and they were found by trying to add ONE more feature to a face that already had three.

found.afro: grizz drew ZERO pixels of skin anywhere on his head. The afro is a single convex ball 1.34r wide centred on the head, and its front surface sat at z 1.14r against a skull surface of 0.82r, so it swallowed eyes, nose and forehead together. Shipped in the same change that added the eyes.
found.glasses: Sat at y -0.03r -- the head's vertical CENTRE, 0.37r above the eyes -- and stood only 0.011r proud of the skull. Four of thirty kids wore an accessory that drew under a pixel. They were positioned against an older face and never re-checked when the eyes moved down.
found.fixedDepth: facingCue placed every feature at an ABSOLUTE z, while the skull's z half-extent is headW * 0.95 and headW runs 0.90-1.08 across the roster. A wide-headed kid's face bulges forward past any constant. The eyes and nose survived it by luck -- still proud on all 30, but by as little as 0.014r -- and a brow at a fixed z is swallowed outright above headW 1.052: the skull front runs 0.884 * headW at the brow's latitude against a fixed brow front of 0.930. That is calls_shot, cricket, sprout and the_prof. Derived from the surface instead, the margin is a constant +0.066r for every kid.
found.brow: The first brow was placed at the anatomical middle of the head and drawn in raw hair colour. Nine of eleven fringes cover that latitude, so it was removed as unshippable. That diagnosis was half right: the position was wrong, the colour was not.

proxyFace.whyItMattered: The cue exists so a clip authored 180 degrees backwards is visible on the review page. A face that is invisible on the widest-headed third of the roster, absent on the afro kid and sub-pixel on the four who wear glasses does not do that -- and the page itself was showing the back of the head anyway (see reviewFacing).
proxyFace.fix: Features are placed by latitude on the head ellipsoid and sunk a fixed fraction of r into its own surface (onSkull), so they move with headW instead of ignoring it -- provably a no-op at headW 1, the same argument the hair re-anchor used. The afro keeps its exact width and top but is pulled back and shallower for the face opening, PLUS a skull-hugging cap for the hairline: pulling a convex ball back far enough to clear the eyes necessarily clears the forehead too, which trades no-face for no-hairline. Glasses moved onto the eyes on the same derivation. The brow is the kid's own hair colour shaded by BROW_SHADE toward the shared cool shadow -- raw hair colour is invisible on pale-haired kids and ink would have vanished into the three near-black hair colours it half-emerges from.
proxyFace.reviewFacing: src/v2/spike/AnimSpike.ts stood the kid at PI*0.82, where the face-toward-camera dot is -0.47: the page that exists to review whether a clip faces the right way was showing the BACK of the head by default, which is why the buried face went unnoticed there. PI*0.5 gives a dot of +0.49 and keeps 0.87 of the lateral travel a dive needs.
proxyFace.pinnedBy: src/v2/render/skeleton.test.ts casts rays along RIGS.PLAY's elevation through every front-facing vertex of a feature and asks whether it is the FRONTMOST surface, keyed on tagged index ranges in the merged geometry. Identity cannot come from colour: the nose is skin-coloured on a skin-coloured head, so a colour test passes with the nose deleted, and eyes, brows and glasses share one ink. Thresholds are RATIOS against the same feature on a bald kid, because each is embedded to a different depth and so has its own healthy value. Head width is varied explicitly, since a fixture built at headW 1 cannot see the defect that only exists above 1.04. Every assertion was verified to FAIL against the code it replaced.
proxyFace.falseNegative: The test proves GEOMETRIC visibility, not perceptual visibility: it would pass a feature fully exposed and one pixel wide. browMinContrast covers the colour half for the brow; nothing covers absolute size, and at the Look Spike's game distance a face is a few pixels by design -- render.characterPresence already records why that cannot be fixed with size.
proxyFace.informs: src/v2/render/ProxyCharacter.ts BROW_SHADE and BROW_MIN_CONTRAST, src/v2/spike/AnimSpike.ts kid facing

runCadence.what: The ground speed each locomotion clip is authored to read correctly at. DERIVED from pace.homeToFirst, not measured -- BB2001 has no on-screen representation of a clip's authored speed, so no frame can be read for it.
runCadence.why: A locomotion clip runs in place while the engine slides the character along the ground, and the engine sets playback rate = simSpeed / authoredSpeed. Without an authored speed there is no number to divide by, and the feet skate at every speed. docs/v2/animation-brief.md originally said only '2.5 strides/sec at 1x speed', which pins CADENCE and says nothing about ground speed.

derivation.anchor: pace.homeToFirst: 4200ms over one 60ft basepath leg (n=3, conformed).
derivation.cadence: The brief's own 24-frame cycle at 30fps is 1.25 cycles/s = 2.5 footfalls/s, which settles the ambiguity in the word 'stride': it meant a single step, and the frame count says so rather than an argument about terminology.
derivation.note: 1.43x body height per step is longer than an elite adult sprinter's step relative to height. Kept deliberately -- the brief asks for cartoon spacing and 'everything slightly too much effort' -- but recorded, because if the proxy reads as skating the fix is a SHORTER CYCLE (18 frames gives a 4.29ft step) and never a slower run. The run speed is the measured quantity; the cadence is the free one.

runCadence.others: run_fast 17.9, trot 7.1, jog_back 8.6, shuffle_left/right 7.2, walk_on 4.4 ft/s. All proportions against the anchor, all unmeasured. Their bands overlap on purpose: pickLocomotion keeps the playback rate inside the brief's 0.6x-1.4x legibility window at every speed the game can produce, which clips.test.ts asserts over the whole range.
runCadence.whatWouldClose: Nothing in BB2001 can close this: an authored playback speed leaves no trace on screen. It could be VALIDATED against our own sim once v2 has baserunning, by measuring foot-contact slip at the rendered speed and requiring it under a threshold.

characterDrawCost.what: A DELIVERED model costs 8 draw calls where a proxy costs 2, and 13 characters put the Look Spike at 122 draws against a budget of 90. LOD pays for itself on triangles in the same measurement (93.3k -> 47.6k, -49%), so the trade is real and one-directional: the character pipeline buys triangles with draw calls.
characterDrawCost.why: ProxyCharacter's header states the budget as '1 mesh + 1 outline hull -- exactly the 2-draw-calls-per-character the perf budget allows'. That sentence is true of a PROXY and was read as a statement about characters. A commissioned model carries the four material slots the asset contract mandates (M_Body / M_Uniform / M_Hair / M_Accessory); three.js splits a multi-primitive mesh into one Mesh per primitive; and the inverted hull needs a sibling per Mesh. 4 x 2 = 8. Neither number was wrong -- they had simply never been measured in the same scene.

measured.how: Look Spike at /v2/?kids=13, PLAY rig, park venue, high tier, toggling forceProxy between reads so nothing else in the scene changed. Rendered SYNCHRONOUSLY from the page: a backgrounded tab stops requestAnimationFrame, which freezes renderer.stats() and is what made the first three readings identical and wrong.

perCharacter.modelNote: 8 is the MAXIMUM -- two draws per POPULATED material slot. The measured total is 76 extra draws over 13 kids, not the 78 that 13 x 6 would predict, because one of the thirteen is bald and so carries no M_Hair primitive at all. The exporter skips empty slots and three.js never makes a Mesh for a primitive that does not exist; an accessory-less kid is 6 the same way.

drift.note: The triangle budget is comfortable in both modes; only draw calls are at risk, and only with models.

characterDrawCost.whatWouldClose: One of: (a) ONE outline hull per LOD level instead of one per primitive -- the inner hulls are entirely hidden behind the character, but merging primitives is only trivial when they share attribute buffers, which a real delivery need not do; (b) fewer material slots per character, which is a contract change that costs either the team-colour multiply or the face atlas; (c) re-derive the 90, which was set against a proxy-only scene and has never been measured on a target device with models on it. Do NOT close it by dropping outlines at distance: a 20px character is where the contour does the most work.
characterDrawCost.informs: src/v2/render/CharacterModel.ts (attachOutline per primitive), src/v2/render/ProxyCharacter.ts (the 2-draw-calls-per-character header claim, now true only of proxies), src/v2/spike/LookSpike.ts (the on-screen budget line)

art.note: Character-art measurements: how BB2001 DRAWS its kids, as opposed to how fast it moves them (pace) or where it puts its camera (geometry).

battingStance.what: How a BB2001 batter HOLDS the bat at rest: where the hands sit, how long the bat is, and how high its tip reaches -- all as fractions of the batter's own body height, so they transfer across sprite scales and into our 200x260 viewBox.
battingStance.why: Reported as 'the batters all look like they hold the bat in the wrong position'. Our stance had never been measured; the code comment asserting it WAS the Backyard silhouette was written by eye, and was wrong on two of the three quantities.

definitions.bodyHeight: feet (lowest body pixel) to crown (highest NON-BAT pixel). Excluding the bat is the whole point -- the bat sticks out past the head in the wrong poses, which is the thing being measured.
definitions.gripHeightFrac: (feet - knobY) / bodyHeight. How high off the ground the hands are.
definitions.batLenFrac: bat length / bodyHeight, from the PCA major axis of the bat's pixels.
definitions.tipAboveHeadFrac: (crownY - tipY) / bodyHeight. POSITIVE means the bat pokes above the head.
definitions.gripDxFrac: (knobX - bodyCentreX) / bodyHeight. How far outboard the hands are.
definitions.degFromVertical: signed angle of the bat's major axis; sign follows the batter's handedness, so compare magnitudes.

battingStance.method: Bat pixels found by EXACT palette match (240,208,164) -- ScummVM's blit is integer nearest-neighbour, so colours survive the capture exactly and no thresholding is needed. Body found by differencing against t=400, a frame of the same behind-plate camera with NO batter in it, then taking the largest connected foreground component and subtracting its bat pixels. Bat axis and endpoints from PCA. The right-edge swing cards draw bats in the SAME wood colour, so the ROI stops at x=520; the HUD strip stops it at y=398.
battingStance.rejectionRule: A frame is rejected if the bat blob is under 800px or under 0.6 body-heights long -- that catches mid-swing frames (the bat blurs off-ROI or foreshortens) and SQUARED/bunt frames, where the bat is held out flat and is NOT the resting stance. Every plate-view screenshot in sources.local is a squared frame, which is why this had to come off the video.
battingStance.nNote: Six at-bats, six different batters, ONE capture and one venue. That is the right shape of evidence for this quantity in a way it would not be for a camera property: a batting stance is a per-character art asset, so sampling batters is what matters and sampling venues is not. Body height varies 166-234px across the six because BB scales the batter sprite per character, which is exactly why every quantity here is a FRACTION and none is a pixel count.
battingStance.theTightOne: tipAboveHeadFrac. Range -0.120..-0.004, and five of six samples sit within 0.006 of exactly level -- BB tops the bat out AT the crown and never above it. That single invariant is most of what makes the stance read as a stance, and it is the one ours broke.
battingStance.degIsPerCharacter: Bat angle is NOT one value: five samples cluster at 7.7-19.9 degrees and Mikey Thomas sits at 48.9. Sampling t=505-512 at 0.5s intervals shows him dead static the whole time, so this is his stance and not a frame of an animation. Bonds by contrast cycles a 3-frame idle waggle across 9.1/9.5/11.2 -- a ~2 degree flutter, which is the scale of the only animation in the resting pose. So we render a per-kid `stance` table rather than one angle, and no band is claimed for degrees.

was.why: Hands at 0.495 were at CHIN height, nearly twice BB's 0.277 -- on a chibi body whose head eats the top 45%, BB's 'chest height' lands near the belt. That put the grip level with the face, which is what forced the near forearm across the chin (its ink reached y=126 against a chin at y=134), and it left the 0.572-length bat pointing straight up past the cap instead of topping out at it. The angle (-6) and outboard offset were already inside BB's bands; height and length were not, and those two are what the eye reads.

battingStance.conformNote: All four fractions now sit inside BB's measured bands, with tipAboveHeadFrac landing on the median exactly. The test DERIVES ours from BAT_STANCE_GEOMETRY rather than restating them, so editing the pose without editing this record goes red. Note it checks front.normal only: the other three stance variants are deliberate per-kid spread across the same bands (BB's own batters spread further), and pinning all four would freeze variation the measurement explicitly found.

batOcclusion.what: WHAT covers a BB2001 batter's bat at rest, and what does not. The companion to art.battingStance: that record fixed where the bat IS, this one fixes what is allowed in front of it.
batOcclusion.why: The stance conformed to art.battingStance on all four fractions and still read wrong on the behind-plate rig. The quantity it was wrong on had never been measured: our rear pose drew the bat as the backmost layer and then put the head on top of a quarter of the barrel. An earlier note in BAT_STANCE claimed 'BB's own bats overlap the head box in all six samples' and moved our grip inboard on that basis -- but a bounding-BOX overlap is not occlusion, and BB has none.

definitions.occludedBandFrac: The lowest and highest points of the bat's axis that are NOT bat-coloured, as fractions of body height above the feet. Same bodyHeight definition as art.battingStance (feet to highest non-bat pixel).
definitions.occludedFrac: Fraction of the sampled axis that is covered by something.
definitions.headCrossesBat: Whether any occluded sample lies under the head rather than the hands/forearms.
definitions.axisClearanceRatio: OUR side. Perpendicular distance from the skull centre to the bat's axis, divided by the skull's half-width. >= 1 means the axis runs outside the skull; < 1 means the head is eating barrel.

batOcclusion.method: Batter and bat segmented exactly as art.battingStance (diff against t=400, the same behind-plate camera with no batter in it; largest connected component; bat by exact palette match on 240,208,164). The bat's major axis comes from PCA; it is then sampled knob->tip and each sample tested for bat colour. The two end samples are dropped -- a PCA endpoint lands a pixel outside the blob and would read as a false occlusion at the tip.
batOcclusion.theFinding: In all six samples the occluded run is CONTIGUOUS and sits between 0.204 and 0.681 of body height -- the hands and forearms on the handle. Above it the bat is unbroken to the tip. Rendering the occluded samples in red over the frame shows the red segment starting under the top fist and ending at the knob, with the barrel passing clear ALONGSIDE the head, its left edge just touching the head silhouette. BB's head never crosses its bat.
batOcclusion.nNote: The same six at-bats as art.battingStance, re-read for a different quantity -- so the sampling argument carries over unchanged: a batting stance is a per-character art asset, and sampling batters is what matters.

The ANCHOR is now measured: pace.homeToFirst is 4200ms at n=3, and our 2113ms is a 49.7% drift -- we run the basepath in half BB's time. measurementTrap.what: Why the obvious automation does not work, recorded so the next pass does not rediscover it.
measurementTrap.finding: Detecting 'the runner reached 1B' from a change-fraction spike in a box on the bag FAILS. BB2001 plays canned fielder animations at the bag, and they are deterministic: six different plays produced change series matching to the millisecond (1.187:0.07, 1.287:0.07, 1.337:0.08, 1.387:0.12, ...). A naive threshold reads six identical 'arrivals'. The tell was the impossible precision -- six unrelated plays cannot agree to 1ms -- and it was caught only because the numbers were inspected rather than aggregated.
measurementTrap.implication: Runner arrival must be distinguished from scripted animation by magnitude AND by the runner's track along the baseline, or read frame-by-frame off a zoomed corridor sheet at the true 50ms period. Either way it is per-play work; it is not a threshold sweep.
measurementTrap.note: This is precisely the failure mode this whole instrument exists to prevent: a plausible, confident, wrong number. It would have produced a home->1B time with a suspiciously tight spread and therefore a HIGH derived confidence.

captureConfounds.what: Why THIS capture (session1) cannot yield clean pace numbers, and what a capture that could must do differently. Found by attempting all three pace metrics on the 14 indexed plays, 2026-07-23.
findings: home->1B lane overlap: in the backyard-grass venue (the only venue any local play is on), the 1B foul line points straight into right-center field. Every ball put in play in this session went to right/center, so the batter-runner's home->1B lane is drawn ON TOP OF the ball-and-fielder action. A frontier tracker along the baseline locks onto the right fielder standing near 1B, not the runner. Clean anchor samples need the ball hit to LEFT field (3B side) or an infield single, so the right-side lane stays empty.

between-pitch is deliberation, not turnaround: the plate-view segments are long (30s+) but the gaps between actual pitches are 5-12s of PLAYER DELIBERATION over the pitch cards (the notes already flag pitch selection as untimed). FLOW.BETWEEN_PITCH_MS models the forced catch->ready dead time (~1.3s), which is a sub-second sliver AFTER each pitch settles -- invisible in the pitch-to-pitch cadence and readable only frame-by-frame per pitch.

few clean flies: the short right porch turns most solid contact into grounders that roll to the fence (play-01 is the type case -- a ball rolling to the wall, retrieved), not arcing flies. FLY_HANG needs deliberate shallow->deep pop-ups, which a natural at-'em playthrough rarely produces.

trackerLessons.what: What actually works for tracking a RUNNER, recorded because the pass burned most of its time rediscovering it. Companion to pace.measurementTrap, which covers why threshold-on-a-box detection fails.
findings: Reduce each moving blob to the BOTTOM-CENTRE of its bounding box, not its centroid. BB draws kids in 3/4 iso, so a change-mass centroid sits at the runner's chest -- which, along the home->1B axis, is ~19px FURTHER up the line than his feet. Centroids systematically overstate progress; sprite origins do not.

Select by sprite SHAPE, not by being the largest change. In the lane, a full kid is 28-44px tall with feet within ~12px of the axis. That one filter rejects both persistent contaminants at once: the floating NAME BUBBLE (13px tall, ~19px off-axis, and it LAGS the runner so it is not a proxy for him) and the first baseman camped on the bag (8-14px on the far side of the axis).

A clean monotone ramp from s=0 to s=leg is the validity check. No canned BB fielder animation produces one, so a low-residual straight-line fit is positive evidence the track is a runner. Correspondingly, a max residual above ~25px means the tracker changed sprites mid-run and the sample must be dropped -- that culled 2 of 5 otherwise plausible home->1B fits here.

Fit a SPEED over the middle of the run rather than differencing two endpoint frames. It averages dozens of frames instead of trusting two, and it degrades gracefully when the runner is briefly occluded.

Annotate the sheet, don't estimate off it. Drawing a fixed box on 1B in every tile turns 'how far along is he?' into 'is he at the box yet?'. That single change is what made the eye reads usable at 400ms steps.

THE TARGET SHADOW IS NOT THE BALL. BB draws a descending indicator on the corridor floor showing where the pitch is headed. It is smooth, monotone, roughly parabolic and survives every motion filter -- i.e. it passes the exact test used to argue a track IS the ball. It is also the object behind the '~930ms descent' that instrument.backgroundSubtraction rejected as 'a shadow'. Rule: on the plate view there are THREE moving things (ball sprite, target indicator, swing cursor); a tracker that has not been shown to separate all three has identified none of them.

TILE SPACING ALIASES BOTH WAYS. At 250ms tiles a sub-300ms flight can fall ENTIRELY BETWEEN TILES and the pitch looks like it never happened; at 33ms tiles on a 22fps source most tiles are duplicates and the extra tiles are false precision. Choose spacing from the DISTINCT frame period (50ms here), never from the container rate, and never finer than the event you are bracketing.

A DOWNSCALED CONTACT SHEET HIDES THE BALL. BB's ball is ~5px in native 640x480; a sheet whose tiles are rendered below 1:1 loses it into the grass. Magnify the corridor crop rather than widening the sheet -- several early 'the ball is not visible here' reads were the sheet's fault, not the game's.

MAGNIFY BEFORE YOU JUDGE A FRAME. This is the big one, and it is four-for-four: BB's original 270ms, the YouTube 250ms, and two of our own re-reads at 180-200ms ALL marked 'release' at the first frame the ball could be spotted. The true flight is ~1230ms. A ~5px ball on textured grass is invisible at 1x and obvious at 2x with flags=neighbor. Any frame judgement made on a downscaled sheet is worthless -- crop tight and scale up FIRST. A corollary trap: at that size a pitcher's ARM reads as a held ball, so 'the ball is still in his hand' is exactly as unreliable as 'the ball is not drawn yet'.

VARIABLE FRAME RATE. macOS screen recordings declare 60fps and deliver something else -- the 2026-07-26 capture holds 49,630 frames across 866s (57.3fps average). Deriving timestamps from frame INDEX would have been ~5% wrong with no symptom. Read time off an in-frame stopwatch, or off PTS, never off frame counting.

pitchCorridor.what: Mound-to-plate flight time, and how it scales with the pitcher's arm.
pitchCorridor.whyThisRecordExists: src/config.ts's PITCH_SPEED block calls itself 'Backyard-measured' and states a ~250ms-to-~700ms corridor. Until 2026-07-24 NO record backed that claim -- it rests on two n=1 readings off the superseded YouTube stream. An in-code comment asserting a measurement that nothing gates is precisely the failure this file exists to prevent, so the claim now has a record even though the answer is still 'not measured'. conformance.test.js enforces the link.
pitchCorridor.whyWithdrawn: Filed 2026-07-25 as conformed/driftPct 0.0 on n=3 hand marks; withdrawn 2026-07-25 after review. Four independent problems, any one of which is disqualifying. (1) THE RELEASE FRAME IS NOT OBSERVABLE FOR THE PITCH TYPE MEASURED. The method's own classification rule is 'a fastball is invisible until late'; you cannot both identify a pitch as a laser BECAUSE the ball is not drawn early and claim to have read the frame it separated from the pitcher. CORRECTED 2026-07-26: an earlier draft of this record said the ball sprite is 'drawn in only ~5 frames'. That was wrong, and wrong the same way -- at low magnification BB's ~5px ball is LOST IN THE GRASS for the first two-thirds of its flight, but it IS drawn from release. Re-read at >=2x magnification the ball is visible leaving the hand. So 'release' was marked at the first frame the ball could be SPOTTED, which is late by construction -- the conclusion stands, the stated evidence did not. (2) THE TARGET SHADOW WAS NOT DISTINGUISHED FROM THE BALL. BB draws a descending target indicator on the corridor floor. It is smooth, monotone and reads exactly like a ball track. instrument.backgroundSubtraction records a ~930ms descent being rejected as 'a shadow'; that object is the target indicator, its span is ~3.5x the recorded flight, and which of the two bounds the flight was never settled. (3) PRECISION EXCEEDS THE SOURCE. instrument.frameRate sets effectiveFramePeriodMs 50 for session2 and warns a ~250ms flight is +-20%% needing n>=5; the corridor was read off a 33ms sheet at n=3 and every value is a round multiple of 10ms. fastballSpread 50 is exactly one frame period, i.e. the tolerance was the noise. (4) THE SAME PITCH IS RECORDED FOUR WAYS. t=53.90 appears as 220ms (capture index), 233ms (this record's own bracket), 234ms (instrument.clockValidity) and 250ms (the sample's ms). clockValidity also records a 100ms gap between last-seen-in-hand and first-seen-airborne -- a +-43%% ambiguity on the start endpoint of a ~230ms quantity, never propagated here.

flyHang.method: BB's LANDING-PREVIEW DISC, not the ball. See instrument.landing-disc for why the ball itself is not trackable here. The disc appears on the frame of contact and vanishes on the frame the flight ends -- verified by eye on all four samples, including one where the ball LANDS rather than being caught, so the disc marks end-of-flight either way.
excluded: play-09 (5383ms) and play-18 (5417ms) are HOME RUNS. Their discs are real and both read ~5.4s, but a ball that leaves the park is not what LIVE.LAUNCH.FLY_HANG_MS models -- our sim decides homers at launch and they never enter the live-play hang. Recorded here rather than silently dropped, and worth noting they are longer than every in-play sample.
play-08 and play-14 draw no landing disc at all. play-14 is an infield pop that BB banners as INFIELD FLY; the disc appears to be an outfield affordance.
flyHang.driftNote: Our flies DO hang long relative to the run, but by 14-38% -- not the 42-106% the superseded n=1 reading implied. And the absolute direction is the opposite of what everyone assumed: BB's flies hang 2.9-5.1s against our 2.0-2.9s, i.e. LONGER than ours. The defect was never that our flies are slow; it is that our RUN is fast.
flyHang.retuneWarning: Fixing LIVE.RUNNER_SPEED alone OVERSHOOTS. At a 4200ms anchor our current 2000-2900ms flies would sit at ratios 0.476-0.690 against BB's 0.685-1.208 -- too SHORT at both ends. To match BB, FLY_HANG_MS has to go UP to about {MIN: 2875, MAX: 5075} at the same time. Note also that BB's range is WIDER than ours (a 1.76x span against our 1.45x), so shallow and deep flies are more different from each other than we make them.
flyHang.conformNote: RETUNED 2026-07-24 to BB's measured range. Note the direction: FLY_HANG_MS went UP (2000-2900 -> 2875-5075), because the long-assumed 'our flies hang too long' defect was really 'our run is too fast'. Fixing RUNNER_SPEED alone would have left flies too SHORT -- the retuneWarning below is what that trap was.

betweenPitch.definition: Ball ARRIVES at the plate -> the PITCHER HAS IT BACK and is ready to throw again. That is the forced beat FLOW.BETWEEN_PITCH_MS models. What follows it in BB is player deliberation over the swing cards, which is not a game constant and is excluded.
betweenPitch.method: Pitches LOCATED by the HUD count pips (a resolved pitch lights one; nothing else does -- mound motion is also produced by the pitcher's idle ball-toss), then each cycle read by eye off a 20-tile mound-to-plate sheet at 250ms. The full beat is visible in one sheet: ball arrives -> call banner -> ball rests at its crossing spot -> catcher returns it -> pitcher has it.
betweenPitch.sampleGranularity: Read at 250ms steps, so each sample carries +-125ms -- 5% of a 2550ms quantity. Fine here; NOT fine for pace.umpCallDelay, which is why that one stays unmeasured.
betweenPitch.driftNote: Ours is 1250ms against BB's 2550ms -- we are 51% fast, almost exactly the 50% the anchor is fast. AND THE RATIO IS ALREADY RIGHT: as a fraction of the home->1B anchor, BB is 0.607 and we are 0.591, a 2.7% difference. So this constant is correctly PROPORTIONED and only wrong in absolute tempo -- unlike fly hang, which is wrong in both. Scaling it by the same factor as RUNNER_SPEED lands it within a few percent of BB with no separate judgement call.
betweenPitch.conformNote: RETUNED 2026-07-24. Was already correctly PROPORTIONED (0.591 vs 0.607) and wrong only in absolute tempo, so it moved with the anchor and now matches outright.

pitchCadence.what: How long the game waits before throwing the next pitch AT the player -- the beat that decides how rushed batting feels.

ours.behaviour: the MOUND idle clock: when the human is pitching and never picks a pitch, the game picks a fastball down the middle for them. Batting is not gated on input at all -- the pitch fires on FLOW.BETWEEN_PITCH_MS, with PLATE_VIEW.CEREMONY animating that wait and any tap skipping it.

pitchCadence.informs: src/config.ts FLOW.BETWEEN_PITCH_MS, PLATE_VIEW.CEREMONY, and the GameScene pitch scheduling

supersedes.was: BB DOES NOT USE A TIMER.
supersedes.why: OVERCLAIM, corrected on the player's report. The footage only showed that the observed gaps (10.7 / 11.6 / 19.5s) never REACHED a clock -- not that none exists. Seth, who has played the game, reports there IS a pitch clock, just long enough that normal play never hits it. Absence of evidence was written up as evidence of absence; the corrected claim is the one the footage actually supports.
supersedes.lesson: A measurement can only bound what it observed. 'No gap reached X' does not license 'there is no X'.

supersedes.was: The clock is a BATTING-side backstop: BB waits for the batter to choose a swing, so we gate the pitch on a swing-card tap.
supersedes.why: WRONG MECHANISM, corrected on the player's report. The long gaps are real, but they are not BB waiting for a swing selection -- they are the between-pitch CEREMONY (catcher throws back, pitcher gets set) playing out, which is skippable, and Seth was skipping it. The clock he was describing is on the PITCHING side. The numbers in `measured` were never wrong; the story told about what produced them was, and the gate built on that story shipped in #24 and is reverted here.
supersedes.lesson: A gap is a duration, not an explanation. Timing footage bounds HOW LONG a beat lasts and says nothing about WHAT fills it -- and an inferred mechanism dressed as a measured one is the more dangerous error, because it inherits the measurement's credibility.

pitchCadence.conformNote: RETUNED 2026-07-25, then re-scoped the same day. The clock now guards only the mound (beginPitchTurn's auto-pick); nothing on the batting side waits for input, so no mode can hang on a tap that never comes. The worst-case mound turn (clock + PITCH_METER_MS + PITCH_AUTO_THROW_MS = 11.9s) stays under NET.ACTION_TIMEOUT_MS, which launchPitchMain's netWaitFor depends on for liveness.

flowCoherence.what: Which FLOW beats the pace retune left behind.
flowCoherence.finding: The 2026-07-24 retune scaled the live-play sim 1.987x and changed exactly ONE FLOW constant -- BETWEEN_PITCH_MS, the one that was measured. Every other between-moments beat is still at the pre-retune tempo: NEW_BATTER_MS 750, CPU_NEW_BATTER_MS 850, CPU_STEP_MS 1100, AFTER_PLAY_MS 1500, AFTER_LIVE_PLAY_MS 1600, HALF_START_MS 1400, RUN_SETTLE_PAD_MS 500, BANNER_HOLD_MS 1100, BIG_BANNER_HOLD_MS 1600, UMP_CALL_DELAY_MS 200.
flowCoherence.implication: So the game now mixes two tempos: live play at the Backyard pace, and every transition around it at the old, faster one. CPU_STEP_MS (the gap between pitches in the half where the HUMAN pitches) is the one most likely to read as rushed, since it was never scaled and is less than half of the retuned BETWEEN_PITCH_MS that governs the other half.
flowCoherence.note: None of these are measured against BB. Scaling them 1.987x would at least make the game internally consistent; measuring them is a separate pass.
